main_text.p: neno hi fiunt strangulatus uteri à putri fe- mine ortus. Si primùm uteri strangulatus, qui à putri femine oritur,esset morbus to- tius substantiæ,profecto solis remedijs,quæ proprietate totius substantiæ, seu(ut non- nulli dicunt) specifica ui agunt, duntaxat soluerétur.Hoc enim iam supra demonstra- tum est rationibus,quas ipsemet Fernelius producit. Sed omnis strangulatus uteri, à quauis causa sit, auxilijs pellitur, quæ suo temperamento, qualitateque manifesta a- gūt.Sunt autem huiusmodi fœtida omnia, ut castoreum,galbanum,assa fœtida, gaga- tes,asphaltum, lucerna extincta, & alia id genus, quæ suo uapore calido,& sicco in alium contrarium, qui ab utero sursum ef- fertur,agunt. Deinde causam eius cōtinen- tem esse frigidam & humidam,non it infi- Cap.5.cias Fernelius,ueluti hinc patet.Si uaporis (ut ibidem inquit)naturam spestemus plu- rimorum uenenorum conditione frigidus is est, & melancholicus.Quod sane confir- mat Galenus libro de Locis affectis,sexto, & de Compositione medicamentorum κα- να ιοῦσι nono.Igitur uteri suffocatio est af- fectus frigidus. page.notes: The "»" marks in the left margin are printed marks (dialogue/quotation markers) beside the lines of the same paragraph; they are not transcribed as text. The "Cap.5." reference is a printed marginal note. Greek in the margin ("κα-" line and "να ιοῦσι") is printed with the hyphenated word "κα-" followed by Greek; the Greek is rendered as read but may be uncertain: "να ιοῦσι" marked as doubtful. The marginal Greek word fragment "κα-" is doubtful.
